judged_text: createEvent still targets destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which credential invokes it; the per-credential calendar selection implemented for Google was not carried over to Office365. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple Office365 hosts, every per-host createEvent call writes to (or fails with 401/404 against) the first host's calendar, so the other hosts' calendars never receive the event — the PR's core requirement is unimplemented for Office365.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `destinationCalendar` an array and updates GoogleCalendarService.createEvent to select the calendar by `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`). However, Office365CalendarService.createEvent still destructures only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and uses that `externalId` to build the `/me/calendars/{id}/events` URL, with no per-credential selection logic. EventManager now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination, but CalendarManager does not pass `externalId` into provider createEvent and instead always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. So for Office365, repeated per-host createEvent calls will still use destinationCalendar[0] (or default), meaning other hosts’ Office365 calendars won’t be targeted correctly—matching the reported collective-booking failure mode.
